data.name: Kokab
data.long_meaning: In Islamic and Arabic mythology, Kokab is the name of the star Alnitak, one of the three stars in the Orion's Belt constellation. data.cultural_impact: The Orion's Belt constellation and the star Kokab have held significant cultural importance in many civilizations throughout history. In ancient Arabic culture, the constellation was known as "Al Jawharat Al Thurayya," which translates to "The Collar of the Lion." The star Kokab was considered one of the three stars in this collar. The constellation and its stars were associated with various myths and legends, and Kokab was often described as a symbol of royalty and power.
data.spiritual_significance: The Islamic name Kokab holds deep spiritual significance for Muslims. According to Islamic tradition, Allah created the universe from the light of the stars in the Orion's Belt constellation, including Kokab. The name Kokab serves as a reminder of Allah's power, wisdom, and infinite knowledge of the universe. Muslims also believe that Allah guides us through the stars in the night sky, and the star Kokab is believed to be a source of divine guidance and inspiration. Overall, the name Kokab inspires awe and reverence for the wonders of Allah's creation.
